{"id":"01a0f903-6a84-7c61-a105-a8a97e1d1398","created":true,"summary":"Releases ship automatically on every merge to main; no release tags"}

With your new process, merging to `main` is the release. There's no separate step:

1. Open a PR against `main`.
2. Get it reviewed and make sure CI passes.
3. Merge it. CI builds and publishes automatically.

Don't push a `vYYYY.MM.N` tag, and don't publish by hand.

The project's stored memory still said releases were cut by pushing a `vYYYY.MM.N` tag. I saved a new memory with your merge-to-main process and marked it as replacing the old one, so later sessions get the current process. The CI config isn't in this repo, so I couldn't check the pipeline itself. The new memory is based on what you told me.
